headline: Two Dutch privacy groups are asking a court to ban sales of Meta's AI glasses in the Netherlands because the glasses can film people without their consent.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a legal move with wider privacy interest, but only a request for a court date so far and the claims are the campaigners'.
importance_line: People who could be filmed without knowing, in places such as toilets, changing rooms and playgrounds, would gain protection if the court agrees, and sales of the glasses in the Netherlands would stop, but no hearing date is set, Meta has not commented and the legal claims are the campaigners' own.
summary: DutchNews.nl reports that the privacy organisations Offlimits and The Firewall are seeking a court injunction against Meta to stop sales of its AI glasses in the Netherlands, arguing that the camera glasses breach Dutch criminal laws against filming people without consent, after Meta did not answer a formal letter sent two weeks ago. They also say the glasses' recording light can be covered and that Meta stores the footage and uses it to train its AI, which they argue is also an offence; this follows our 3 Oct 2026 edition, which carried Business Insider's report that the Dutch retailers Hans Anders and Wehkamp paused sales.
notes: DutchNews.nl full text read. Follow-up of our 3 Oct 2026 edition (Dutch retailers paused sales) and 5 Oct 2026 edition (Norway proposes a temporary ban). Meta has not commented.
